name: Lower Morehead
confidence_why: The only statement on record is Wurm's 1971 remark, made at the level of the whole Tonda sub-family from his own brief Lower Morehead fieldnotes, that these languages have a fairly complex stress system with rhythm principles and no tone, with no placement rule given, and none of the other works read (Ray 1907, Ray 1923, Wurm 1975, Evans 2012, Grummitt and Masters 2012, Döhler 2018, Carroll 2020) says anything about stress in this language.

Wurm (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 115-172. Canberra: Research School of Pacific Studies, ANU. Open access: ANU Open Research hdl 1885/254300.
catalog_locator: p. 156, §3.35.12.3 'Typological and Structural Features of the Languages of the Tonda Sub-Family'
catalog_quote: The present writer has at his disposal information on the structure of Tonda, and some brief notes on that of Lower Morehead (Peremka) from his own fieldnotes, on Upper Morehead (Rouku) from A. Capell's fieldnotes, and on Kanum from Drabbe's (1954) and Boelaars' (1950) publications. The languages are virtually identical in structure, though Kanum appears to differ somewhat from the other three in phonology. The phonology of the languages of the Tonda Sub-Family is rather complex, though perhaps somewhat less so than that of those of the Nambu Sub-Family. ... Vowel length is phonemic. A considerable number of diphthongs are found, but clusters of more than two vowels seem to be absent. The suprasegmental system appears to manifest itself as a fairly complex stress system with rhythm principles, but no tonal system appears to be present. The syllable structure seems to be somewhat less complex than in the Nambu Sub-Family, but shows more complicated syllable-boundary clustering.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule exists for Kánchá in any source. Wurm's subgroup-level remark (which explicitly draws on his own brief fieldnotes on Lower Morehead = Kánchá) says only that Tonda languages have a 'fairly complex stress system with rhythm principles' and no tone. The nearest first-hand description of a member of the same dialect chain is Döhler 2018: 71 for Komnzo: primary stress on the initial syllable of the phonological word (trochee/dactyl/ditrochee templates), with exceptions for partial reduplication and verbal proclitics; that is a Komnzo statement, not a Kánchá one.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing for Kánchá. Komnzo (Döhler 2018: 71): secondary stress only in words of more than three syllables, on the third syllable of most five-syllable words and the fourth of most six/seven-syllable words; 'remains to be investigated'.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for Kánchá. Komnzo exceptions to initial stress: partial reduplication (first syllable unstressed, rrokar [rə̆ˈrokar]) and verbal proclitics (bŋatrakwr [bə̆ˈŋatrakʷə̆r]).
new_statements.domain_note: Wurm's statement is about the Tonda Sub-Family as a whole (Tonda, Lower Morehead/Peremka, Upper Morehead/Rouku, Kanum), based on fieldnotes he calls 'brief' for Lower Morehead; it establishes stress-not-tone but not the word-level placement. Döhler's initial-stress rule is for the phonological word in Komnzo (Rouku village), a sister variety in the Anta-Komnzo-Wèré-Kémä-Kánchá dialect chain (Döhler 2018: 41-42; Carroll 2020: 2); it must not be transferred to Kánchá without a Kánchá source.
new_statements.identity_note: Kánchá [kunj1246, ISO pep] = Kunja = Lower Morehead = Peremka (Wurm 1971/1975; Ray 1923 'Wandatok'we' villages Tumgaka/Perem) = Kénzä/Kámundjo Tjokwasi/Wartha (ethnographers' names); dialects Kánchá and Kémä (Wikipedia/Ethnologue; Döhler 2018 has 'very little data on Kémä'). Wurm's 1971 statement covers the whole Tonda Sub-Family (Tonda, Lower Morehead, Upper Morehead = Komnzo/Wára/Anta/Arammba [wara1294 etc.], Kanum). Döhler's initial-stress rule is for Komnzo (wara1294 Anta-Komnzo-Wára-Wérè-Kémä, Rouku village), a sister variety in the same dialect chain, not Kánchá.

sources.note: §1.4 (pp.37-42) compares the Tonda varieties incl. Kánchá [kə̆ⁿdza] (segmental correspondences, lexicostatistics from Wurm 1971 and Clifton et al. 1991, case/pronoun/verb morphology) but gives no stress data for Kánchá; states Kánchá, Wèré, Komnzo, Wára, Anta form one dialect chain. §2.4.5 p.71 (Komnzo only): 'Primary stress.. is assigned to the initial syllable of a word'; exceptions partial reduplication and verbal proclitics; secondary stress only in 4+-syllable words; stress correlates intensity/pitch, not duration.
